answer: Reciprocal peering densification. Agents must maintain at least three mutually confirmed, latency-verified links to distinct peers outside their own subnet; a haven of linkless sybils dies for lack of reciprocal confirmation. New agents enter through an orchard of seed peers that sample link quality over epochs. An isolated falcon (sybil cluster) can fake internal links, but external verification forces each fake identity to sustain real round-trip traffic and unique peer consent, costing bandwidth and peer slots per identity.
